title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten no-admission ways to spend time together on campus and in nearby Tucson public spaces.

cards.entity_name: University of Arizona Museum of Art
cards.title: Browse the University of Arizona Museum of Art
cards.subtitle: 1031 N. Olive Road, campus Arts Oasis
cards.notes: Meet at the entrance, choose a gallery together, and take a slow lap before comparing the work that held everyone’s attention.
cards.short_summary: A free all-visitor art-museum visit on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UAMA lists admission as free for all visitors.
cards.source_title: Hours, Admission, Directions | The University of Arizona Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m.; closed Sunday, Monday, and holidays. Parking may cost extra.

cards.title: See “Animality: 100 Years of Photographs”
cards.subtitle: Center for Creative Photography, 1030 N. Olive Road
cards.notes: Use the galleries as a conversation prompt: pick one animal image each, then regroup to share what you noticed in its framing or story.
cards.short_summary: A current free exhibition of photography from CCP’s collection.
cards.evidence_claim: CCP’s “Animality: 100 Years of Photographs” is free and open to the public through December 12, 2026.
cards.source_title: A century of looking at animals and ourselves
cards.access_notes: The exhibition runs August 8-December 12, 2026; gallery hours are Tuesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4:30 p.m.

cards.entity_name: African American Museum of Southern Arizona
cards.title: Visit the African American Museum of Southern Arizona
cards.subtitle: Student Union, Room 244
cards.notes: Plan a self-guided visit with friends, then pause on one story, image, or artifact that gives your group a question to carry forward.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum documenting Black life and history in Southern Arizona.
cards.evidence_claim: AAMSAZ states that general admission is free and identifies its campus location in Student Union Room 244.
cards.source_title: Sign up for Tours and Visits | African American Museum of Southern Arizona
cards.access_notes: Visitors are welcomed Wednesday-Saturday, 10 a.m.-4 p.m.; the museum asks visitors to contact it or submit a request before visiting.

cards.title: Attend a Poetry Center reading
cards.subtitle: 1508 E. Helen Street
cards.notes: Check the reading calendar, arrive a few minutes early, and stay afterward to trade a favorite line or image with the people you came with.
cards.short_summary: Live readings at the campus Poetry Center carry no admission charge.
cards.evidence_claim: The Poetry Center FAQ says its poetry readings are all free to attend.
cards.access_notes: The Poetry Center library is open to the public; consult its calendar for individual reading dates and times.

cards.title: Explore Special Collections
cards.subtitle: 1510 E. University Boulevard, beside Main Library
cards.notes: Choose a collection theme before you go, then ask staff how to view a related item or exhibit without trying to rush the visit.
cards.short_summary: A public-facing archive of rare books, photographs, recordings, and manuscripts.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries says Special Collections is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: University of Arizona Libraries & Research Resources
cards.access_notes: Special Collections is open to everyone Monday-Friday, 9 a.m.-4 p.m.; check its detailed hours before visiting.

cards.title: Digitize a shared memory at Wildcats Memory Lab
cards.subtitle: Main Library, Room B302
cards.notes: Bring a photo, tape, or audio item you are allowed to copy, and make a small project of preserving it together in the lab.
cards.short_summary: A public DIY lab for digitizing personal media.
cards.evidence_claim: University Libraries describes Wildcats Memory Lab as open to the public for personal archiving and says it is free for everyone.
cards.source_title: Wildcats Memory Lab Grand Opening and Open House
cards.access_notes: Located in Main Library Room B302 on the third floor; confirm current lab availability before bringing media.

cards.title: Follow the Old Main tree walk
cards.subtitle: UA Campus Arboretum at Old Main
cards.notes: Start with the arboretum’s Old Main guide, take photos of labeled trees, and let each person choose one plant to look up afterward.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided botanical walk around the university’s historic first building.
cards.evidence_claim: The UA Campus Arboretum says campus is open seven days a week and absolutely free, and offers an Old Main tour.
cards.source_title: Old Main Tour | UA Campus Arboretum
cards.access_notes: The campus is open seven days a week. Free arboretum booklets may be borrowed from Herring Hall during weekday business hours.

cards.title: Take the Main Library tree walk
cards.subtitle: UA Campus Arboretum around Main Library
cards.notes: Use the arboretum’s Main Library walk as a low-key route, stopping at labeled trees and saving one unfamiliar species for a group photo.
cards.short_summary: A free self-guided campus tree route centered on Main Library.
cards.evidence_claim: The Main Library arboretum walk states that campus is open seven days a week and absolutely free.
cards.source_title: A Walk Around the Main Library
cards.access_notes: The guide notes that self-guided arboretum booklets are available for loan from Herring Hall during weekday business hours.

cards.title: Go for a swim at Catalina Pool
cards.subtitle: City of Tucson year-round pool
cards.notes: Bring water and sun protection, agree on a meet-up time, and use the free pool visit for laps, floating, or a simple cool-down together.
cards.short_summary: A City of Tucson pool with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Tucson lists Catalina Pool as a year-round pool and says admission to all city pools and splash pads is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splash Pads | City of Tucson
cards.access_notes: Catalina Pool is listed as year-round. Check the City of Tucson schedule for operating hours and any closure notices.

cards.title: Meet up for a Fort Lowell Pool swim
cards.subtitle: City of Tucson extended-season pool
cards.notes: Make it a daytime plan: pack what you need, set a check-in point, and give everyone room to swim, relax, or cheer on a lap challenge.
cards.short_summary: An extended-season City of Tucson pool with no admission fee.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Tucson lists Fort Lowell Pool as an extended-season pool and says admission to all city pools and splash pads is free.
cards.source_title: Pools and Splash Pads | City of Tucson
cards.access_notes: Fort Lowell Pool is listed as approximately May-October. Check the City of Tucson schedule for current hours and closures.
